Recent progress and trends

The Japanese half marathon all-time top lists reflect a marked acceleration in performance standards in recent years, most prominently on the men's side. The breakthrough of multiple sub-60 minute performances in 2025 represented a historic milestone, with the national record lowered to 59:27 at the Marugame Half Marathon.

This surge has dramatically increased the quantity of elite marks, with the all-time lists now featuring 94 performances under 1:01 (as of early 2026), the majority recorded in recent years amid heightened depth at domestic competitions. The Marugame Half Marathon has been instrumental in this development, consistently producing fast times through strong fields and favorable conditions.
Prior to the mid-2010s, improvements were more incremental, with far fewer athletes reaching sub-1:01 levels and limited evidence of sustained depth.

Women's performances have also advanced, albeit at a slower pace, with additional sub-1:08 marks added to the all-time lists in 2024 and 2025. These gains continue to build on established benchmarks while highlighting ongoing progress in Japanese distance running overall.

The all-time top 10 half marathon performances by Japanese women, as compiled in the World Athletics database, highlight a blend of enduring records from the mid-2000s and notable recent improvements.
Progression of the national record

The Japanese women's half marathon national record has been improved twice in the modern era, with both advances occurring in mixed-gender races and representing key milestones in Japanese distance running.

As of early 2026, the World Athletics all-time top list for Japanese men's half marathon performances includes approximately 98 entries (including ties), of which 94 are under 1:01:00.

The distribution shows a marked concentration in recent years, particularly in 2025 and 2026, when a substantial proportion of these performances were recorded, underscoring the rapid progress in Japanese men's elite half marathon running.
Many of these sub-1:01 times have been achieved at domestic events, with the Marugame Half Marathon serving as a prominent venue.

These performances have been achieved by five different athletes. Three of the marks came in the 2000s, demonstrating early elite-level capability, while the remaining three occurred more recently in the 2010s and 2020s, indicating a pattern of steady, if gradual, improvement over time.

This reflects consistent progress among Japanese women at the elite level, though without the dramatic surge seen in recent men's performances. Several of these sub-1:08:00 marks have come at the Marugame Half Marathon.
Earlier, on 2 February 2020, Yusuke Ogura set a then-national record of 1:00:00 at the same venue, underscoring Marugame's long-standing role in national record progressions.

List updates and verification process

The World Athletics all-time top lists for half marathon performances by athletes of Japanese nationality are maintained and updated on an ongoing basis through the verification processes conducted by World Athletics statisticians.

New performances are incorporated into the lists once competition results are submitted from events on the Global Calendar, processed, and confirmed to meet eligibility requirements, such as occurring on certified courses with valid measurements and reported gun times.

That same day saw Kotaro Shinohara clock 59:30 for the second-fastest Japanese time ever, marking the first occasion of multiple sub-60-minute runs by Japanese men and making Ota the first Asian athlete to break the one-hour barrier.

I have participated in various marathons in Japan, from 10km to full marathons, but since this was my first time participating in a marathon in America, I discovered many similarities and differences compared to Japanese marathons, so I will write about them!
1. What is the San Francisco Marathon?
The San Francisco Marathon is a marathon held in late July that tours the northern coastal area of San Francisco.
There are 7 types of races: a 1km kids run, 5km, 10km, half (two types that split the full course), full, and ultra (two laps of the full course).
